part_title: Lambda Monitoring, Use Cases, Runtimes and Event Triggers

scenes.title: Example: Transaction Rate Alarm
scenes.narration: Suppose an application records the number of transactions completed every minute. During normal operation, that metric stays within an expected range. Now imagine a burst of failures or an unexpected drop in completed transactions. Rather than discovering this from customer complaints, publish a meaningful CloudWatch metric and configure an alarm for the relevant threshold and evaluation periods. Trace the response: CloudWatch evaluates the recent datapoints, changes the alarm state when the configured condition is met, and triggers a notification or another supported response. It is important to decide whether a single noisy minute should raise an alarm or whether several consecutive periods are necessary. For an AI-backed checkout assistant, also monitor timeouts, Bedrock throttles and the age of any pending processing queue. A notification tells us that a condition occurred; logs and traces tell us why. The exam distinction is between recording a metric, evaluating an alarm and actually investigating the root cause.

scenes.title: Why Not Just Run a Server?
scenes.narration: Compare a small function that runs only when a customer uploads a document with a server kept running twenty-four hours a day. On the always-on server, the team manages instance size, operating-system patches, capacity and idle time. Lambda starts execution when an event arrives and charges according to its pricing model, so intermittent jobs can be operationally simpler. But that does not make Lambda superior for every workload. Imagine a container processing a large video for ninety minutes: Lambda has a maximum execution duration, so the task belongs in another compute service or needs to be split into bounded stages. An interactive request may also experience initialization delay, and a burst of requests can hit concurrency limits or overload the downstream Bedrock API. Use the comparison to decide from evidence: How long does each job run? How predictable is demand? What latency must users tolerate? What state must persist between requests? These answers, not the word serverless, determine the architecture.

scenes.title: Main Uses of Lambda
scenes.narration: Think about four different Lambda entry points. First, an API Gateway route invokes a function when a browser requests an order summary. Second, an S3 object notification starts work after a document arrives. Third, an SQS event source mapping polls messages and delivers batches for background processing. Fourth, a schedule can invoke a periodic maintenance function. The processing code may look similar, but delivery and failure behavior are not the same. A synchronous API caller expects a response or error while waiting. SQS messages remain available for retry until successfully handled and deleted according to the event source mapping's behavior. This is why a function must identify its event source and use a suitable error strategy. In a GenAI pipeline, Lambda is a good place to validate payloads, prepare retrieval requests, run bounded model calls and store results. If the task needs many dependent steps or prolonged execution, hand off to an orchestrated workflow instead of building an invisible state machine inside one function.

scenes.title: Lambda Supported Languages
scenes.narration: A Lambda function can be written using a supported managed runtime or packaged with a custom runtime or container image. Consider a developer choosing between Python for document-processing libraries and Node.js for a lightweight API handler. Both can receive an event, validate its contents and call AWS services with the relevant SDK. The important differences are practical: dependency compatibility, package size, initialization speed and the team's ability to test the deployment. A native library compiled for the wrong architecture may work on a laptop and fail after deployment. A large package may also increase startup work, even if the handler itself is small. Keep libraries pinned and build for the actual target runtime and architecture. Notice that choosing a language does not bypass Lambda execution limits, IAM authorization or logging requirements. The function's entry point and the permissions granted to its role are separate from the language in which its logic is written.

scenes.title: Lambda Triggers
scenes.narration: Start with the question: who initiates the Lambda execution? With API Gateway, a client sends an HTTP request and typically waits for a synchronous result. With S3 event notifications, a new object can cause asynchronous processing after upload. With SQS or Kinesis, an event source mapping polls the underlying queue or stream and invokes the function with one or more records. Follow the flow in each case rather than treating every trigger as identical. An API timeout affects the waiting user, while a failed queue batch may be delivered again and a stream shard can be affected by repeated failures. The trigger choice therefore determines batch handling, retries, response expectations and possible duplicates. For an AI document pipeline, we might accept an upload quickly, publish a work message, and let a Lambda consumer process the document at a controlled rate. If the model service throttles requests, the queue provides a buffer and the consumer can retry safely using a document or job identifier.
